title: NASA Signs
slide_intent: Show designers how an interior sign system can guide someone from corridor to room and still accommodate a change in destination, occupant or event.
strategic_value: NASA can keep permanent directions recognizable while allowing names, room status and temporary messages to change without replacing a whole installation.
demonstration: The sheet groups interior signs by purpose. Modular overhead directions, floor directories and room plaques appear above a building directory, movable information sign, symbols and access restrictions.
practical_value: Choose which part of a sign must last and which part must be replaceable. A sliding room-name panel calls for a different construction from a permanent identifier.

content_islands.name: Interior principles
content_islands.spec: Place the title and columns of guidance at the top. Specify normally spaced Helvetica for directional reading and mounting appropriate to the architecture.

content_islands.name: Directions and identification
content_islands.spec: Group overhead and wall directions with the floor directory. Alongside them, show the room and desk identifiers, including changeable occupancy and name panels.

content_islands.name: Information and restrictions
content_islands.spec: Use a lower band for the building directory, movable notice, pictograms and regulatory signs. Keep each lettered sign keyed to its description.
